name: Omar Quinn

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. How does an ordinary day at your firm go?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I begin with invoices from building firms, many sent as phone photos from site. I use AI to flag repeats, then compare the pictures with the accounts before I prepare a tax return. I am 43, with a bachelor’s degree and a professional accountancy qualification, and know this work reasonably well; I like solving a missing-payment puzzle, but chasing unreadable photos can fill the afternoon.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and how do you use AI now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Nadia repairs clothes for customers, and our children Leena and Ben are both in school. We have a mortgage, my pay is typical for accounting, and we have around four months of expenses saved with some similar firms nearby. I use AI tools every day, but I keep the source photo open before I tell my supervisor Inez a number is right.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The builders would still send a blurry photo of the bill instead of the bill itself. A small tool would help me find the duplicate, not the missing page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team that AI saves time on sorting supplier invoices if we keep a source link for each figure. I already use it daily to flag repeats, then I check the original before filing a return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my normal salary and mortgage payment to carry on. We have about four months of expenses saved and some accounting firms nearby, so this mild picture does not make my own job feel threatened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the same building-company accounts and my daily AI checks. I would transfer forty from each monthly pay cheque into our emergency account until it covers six months, while keeping the children’s music lessons.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about income here. The blurry invoices still annoy me more than the software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens when a duplicate flag is wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I open both source images and sometimes find two different delivery dates on the same supplier form. I correct the flag and tell my supervisor Inez why I kept both.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why six months rather than four?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Nadia earns from repairing clothes, and the shop can have slow weeks. Forty from my pay is new money toward the mortgage buffer, not a claim that savings grow by magic.

say: I would praise **duplicate flags** only when a source image supports them.
I would tell colleagues I **check originals** before filing returns.
think: Our **four-month cushion** and typical pay cover the mortgage in this picture.
Nadia’s clothing repairs can have **slow weeks**, so I still want more cash.
do: Keep building-company **accounts** and daily AI checks with source images.
Transfer **forty monthly** from salary until six months are saved.
feel: I feel **calm** about my work and pay.
S0.quote: The blurry invoices still annoy me more than the software.
fieldNote: He uses AI **every day** but has found apparently duplicate supplier forms with different delivery dates.
His new **forty-monthly deposit** recognises variable household shop income without predicting a job loss.

steps.text: Keep checking building-company accounts with AI and source images
Transfer forty monthly from salary until reserve covers six months

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Supplier invoices and first tax drafts are right in the path of this change. I would want to set the tool up carefully before anyone changes my hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to test invoice matches on old files with known mistakes. If the tool works, I would still insist on a named accountant for the return and a trainee seeing the bad matches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the firm may cut my own account-checking hours when AI can draft more returns. Four months of savings helps, but Nadia’s tailoring income changes week by week and cannot reliably carry the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask Inez to approve a paid pilot on fifty old supplier files, then configure the approved AI checker with a source-image rule if the test passes. If my paid hours fall in the first year, I would apply only to posted accountant vacancies with a written salary, hours, and start date that cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about fewer paid hours. Doing the work faster could still mean fewer paid hours for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use live client files in the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we would remove names and compare the tool with files whose errors are already known. I would not switch the live workflow until Inez signs off the test report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Inez refuses the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the current accounts and my existing AI checks on approved tools while drawing my normal salary. I would not buy a private subscription to force the change.

say: I would request a **fifty-file pilot** before setting a new workflow.
I would keep a **named signer** and show trainees mistaken matches.
think: My own **checking hours** could shrink even if the new tool works well.
Nadia’s variable shop income cannot reliably carry the **mortgage and children** alone.
do: Run a **paid anonymised pilot** only if Inez approves; otherwise keep current accounts, approved AI checks and normal pay.
Configure the approved **AI checker** with source-image rules only after the test passes.
Apply for **posted accounting work** after hours fall only with written mortgage-covering terms.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my paid hours.
S1.quote: Doing the work faster could still mean fewer paid hours for me.
fieldNote: He proposes **testing and configuration** on known old errors, not a training course.
The pilot needs **paid approval**, while any employer move needs a posted role and written wage, hours, and start date.

steps.text: Run paid fifty-file anonymised pilot only if Inez approves
Configure approved AI checker only if pilot passes and Inez signs off
After first-year hour cuts, take posted accounting job with written mortgage-covering pay, hours and start date
Keep current accounts and approved AI checks at normal salary if pilot refused

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years is not enough for a small firm to rebuild its client list. The robots around 2031 would arrive after the accounting screen is hit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say clients need a named person to answer for a tax return when AGI handles accounts in 2028. I would tell colleagues the field crews may have three more years before capable robots, but our desks do not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my account-checking post or most of its wage to go. Our four-month reserve is useful, but Nadia’s clothing-repair shop cannot cover the mortgage and two children by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now we would defer the planned kitchen refit and I would deposit its monthly saving into a job-loss account. If my firm ends my post in the first year after 2028, I would take a posted paid site-invoice checker job only if its written wage, hours, and start date cover the mortgage and school pickup; I would keep applying for salaried accounting work while that temporary contract lasts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the expected salary loss. A paid site-invoice contract would be a short bridge, but its checking work faces AGI in 2028 too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Nadia?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner Nadia that the old kitchen can wait while we add cash from each pay cheque. We would not put a new loan beside the mortgage now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use all four months to fund a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would keep that cash for the mortgage. I would study the professional body’s free tax updates after work while the current salary lasts.

say: I would insist on a **named tax signer** in 2028.
I would say **2031 robots** give field crews more time than accountants.
think: I expect my **checking wage** to vanish or shrink sharply.
Nadia’s shop cannot replace my share of the **mortgage**.
do: Defer the **kitchen refit** and deposit its planned monthly cost into cash.
After **job loss**, take posted site checking only with written mortgage-covering terms; keep applying for salaried accounting work.
Study **free tax updates** while the present salary continues.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely loss of my salary.
S2.quote: A paid site-invoice contract would be a short bridge, but its checking work faces AGI in 2028 too.
fieldNote: His **site-invoice contract** is still thinking work exposed to 2028 AGI, so only a real paid temporary opening counts.
He protects the **four-month reserve** and funds new cash deposits by delaying the kitchen refit.

steps.text: Defer kitchen refit and deposit its monthly cost into job-loss savings
After layoff, take posted site job with written mortgage-covering wage, school-compatible hours and start date
Keep applying for salaried accounting work while temporary site contract lasts
Study free professional tax updates while keeping current accounting salary

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to see which builders still want a person at the desk. I could make my client calls more useful without leaving the firm yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to keep a paid apprentice path for checking old tax mistakes before 2031. AGI reaches the accounts desk then, and robots around 2034 will later reach the crews on site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect routine tax fees to shrink, but I could become better at explaining supplier disputes to owners. I would not count on that work surviving AGI unless someone budgets a real role for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Inez for paid time to sit on one supplier dispute call each month, and take the calls only if she assigns them. I would transfer forty from monthly pay into cash; in the first year after 2031 I would take a posted client-accounts liaison role only if written wage, hours, and start date cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the later loss of checks, with enough warning to build proof of what clients will pay for. I would keep my present salary if no liaison place is posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn on those calls?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would listen for how Inez gets a builder to find the right invoice without losing the relationship. If she cannot give me paid call time, I would use the firm’s free sample cases while keeping my current accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you borrow for a new certificate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would not spend our mortgage cushion on a certificate. I want supervised paid calls and an advertised wage, not a wall of course badges.

say: I would ask for a **paid apprentice path** before 2031.
I would say **2034 robots** are later than the account-desk change.
think: A funded **liaison post** matters more than a claim that clients like human calls.
do: Learn on **paid supplier calls** only if Inez assigns them; use free cases while employed otherwise.
Transfer **forty monthly** from wages into cash.
Take **posted liaison work** after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering terms.
feel: I feel **anxious**, with time to test client demand.
S3.quote: I want supervised paid calls and an advertised wage, not a wall of course badges.
fieldNote: His learning is **supervised paid calls**, with free cases and existing salary as fallback.
He seeks a **budgeted liaison opening** and written terms before changing employers or roles.

steps.text: Learn through paid supplier calls only if Inez assigns them; otherwise study free cases while employed
Transfer forty monthly from salary into cash reserve
After 2031, take posted liaison job only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours and start date

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would take the children nearer to leaving school. I could build a longer reserve without betting the house on one software plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients AGI reaches accountants’ screens in 2036 and robots reach hands-on site work around 2039. The firm has time to keep apprenticeships and real review files open for juniors.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect basic return fees to fall by 2036, but a decade lets me test whether supplier calls remain paid work. My normal pay and four-month cushion look secure for the near term.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep reviewing the present builder accounts and transfer forty from salary each month until we have eight months saved. I would shadow supplier calls on paid time only if Inez assigns them; if my accounting post contracts in the first year after 2036, I would take a posted liaison position only with written pay, hours, and a start date covering the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant desk change, but not about next month’s bills. I could make a real decision from invoices and offers rather than a sales demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a new system yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would use approved firm tools and keep the household reserve for our mortgage. A tool should earn its cost before it gets a place in our budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Leena and Ben that learning a tool is useful only if you can check its work. I would still encourage them to learn a trade from a person.

say: I would name **2036** as the desk-work date and 2039 for robots.
I would support **paid apprenticeships** with real review files.
think: A longer **reserve** and paid calls could give us a choice.
do: Keep **builder accounts** and shadow paid supplier calls only if Inez assigns them.
Transfer **forty monthly** until eight months are saved.

feel: I feel **uneasy** about future work, with near-term income safe.
S4.quote: A tool should earn its cost before it gets a place in our budget.
fieldNote: His long plan uses **fresh monthly pay deposits**, while preserving the mortgage reserve.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could remove the account-checking pay our mortgage needs. A posted paid role, a short income bridge if the search takes longer than our savings, and funded time on real client calls would help. I would keep working while the present wage lasts.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who will train the next accountant when the tool catches the easy errors. A junior needs to see a bad invoice before the checker turns it green. I would keep the old files available for learning.

headlineQuote: A junior needs to see a bad invoice before the checker turns it green.
portrait: Omar is a **43-year-old** experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who serves building firms.
He has **typical pay**, four months saved, a partner with variable clothing-repair income, two children, and a mortgage.
He uses **AI daily** but checks flags against source photos before filing tax returns.
A **2028** desk shock alarms him; a posted site-invoice contract is also exposed thinking work and only a temporary paid bridge.
Longer warnings allow **paid supplier calls** and fresh monthly saving while he keeps current wages.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his account-checking wage before another paid role begins.
whatWouldHelp: He needs a **posted paid role**, funded client practice, and a short income bridge if savings run out.
